findings.element: PT · Invoices tab · RevRec lock: 'Change Schedule start date instead →' escape route and the note 'When Schedule start is Payment date, this control can be changed.'
findings.finding: The suggested way out of the lock goes in a loop: after the user sets Schedule start to Payment date as the note says, the Invoice date select on PT is still disabled and the lock message still shows.
findings.user_impact: A user who follows the guidance exactly comes back to the same locked control with no explanation and cannot finish the primary task of changing Invoice date.
findings.suggested_fix: Base the PT lock on the current Schedule start value, so the select is enabled and the lock message is gone once Schedule start = Payment date.

evidence.action: PT · RevRec lock → click 'Change Schedule start date instead →' → RevRec: pick Payment date → Confirm → go back to PT · RevRec lock
evidence.observed: Select disabled=true and lock message visible=true; the state map records 'The lock is a fixed variant, not derived from Schedule start.'

findings.element: RevRec · Schedule details table, Schedule start cell of row sub_after_release_3c1b
findings.finding: After the user confirms a new Schedule start date, the Schedule start cell of an existing schedule is rewritten, even though the confirmation modal just said existing schedules keep their dates.
findings.user_impact: The user can't tell what the change actually does, which is half of the primary task, and may think existing schedules were re-dated into another period.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave the Schedule start of existing schedule rows unchanged after confirm, so the table matches the modal's going-forward-only message.

evidence.action: RevRec: pick Invoice issued date → Confirm; then pick Payment date → Confirm
evidence.observed: sub_after_release_3c1b Schedule start changed from '28 Dec 2025' to '6 Jan 2026', then to 'Payment date'; the modal text said 'Existing recognition schedules keep their current dates.'

findings.element: PT · Invoices tab (and Sales tab): Invoice date / Payment posting date select vs the tab's Update button
findings.finding: The select saves itself on change ('Saved' toast), but the same tab also has an Update button that saves ('Settings updated'), so two save models sit side by side on one screen.
findings.user_impact: Users can't tell whether they still need to click Update. They may click it for nothing, or assume the toggles save on change too, and lose edits.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one save model per tab: either the date select waits for Update like the other settings, or the Update button goes and every row saves on change.

evidence.action: Invoices tab (pt-pro): change Invoice date to Created date, then click Update
evidence.observed: Change → toast 'Saved' straight away; Update → a second toast 'Settings updated'. The same pattern is recorded on the Sales tab (Payment posting date 'Saved' plus an Update button).

findings.element: PT · Invoices tab · Pro: Invoice date row and its initial value
findings.finding: The row opens with Issued date selected, but the caption right under it says existing connections stay on Created date, and nothing tells the user which case this connection is.
findings.user_impact: An existing-connection user may think their books have already been re-dated to Issued, or may doubt whether the shown value is real. That undermines their understanding of the current state before they choose.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the selected value match the connection's actual default, so an existing connection shows Created date, and remove the generic default caption.

evidence.action: Open variant pt-pro and read the Invoice date row
evidence.observed: initial_value 'issued'. The caption reads 'New Stripe connections default to Issued date. Existing connections stay on Created date until you change them.' The state map notes 'the state does not say whether this is a new or existing connection.'

findings.element: PT · Invoices tab · Pro: Invoice date row (New badge, help sentence, defaults caption, blue info callout)
findings.finding: One two-option select carries three separate text blocks plus a badge, which outweighs the control itself and the four rows below it.
findings.user_impact: Expert users have to read several paragraphs to find a single select, and the key point (accounting date follows this setting, the table always shows created) is buried in the third block.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut the row to a label and one short help line, and drop the defaults caption and info callout.

evidence.action: Open variant pt-pro and read the Invoice date row
evidence.observed: visible_text shows the help sentence, the defaults caption, and an info callout starting 'The Synder transactions table always shows the invoice created date…'. The state map notes 'three text blocks for one select.'

gaps: Sync info / transaction drilldown is not in the prototype, so I could not check whether the user can see the issued date and the accounting date when they differ from created (FDD S1.5).
There is no trial or new-connection variant, so I could not check the default-value state for new connections or availability on trial.
The 'Upgrade plan' link (below-Pro PT and Summary) and the 'Learn more →' / 'How to change mode' links all have href=#, so I could not check whether the gated user's upgrade path ends in a dead end.
No save-failure, loading or error state was recorded for any auto-save select or for Schedule start Confirm, so I could not check state clarity on failure.
The Summary 'Plan state' segmented control sits inside the product card. The map does not say whether this is prototype chrome or meant as product UI, so I did not judge its affordance.
